title: A valid carried martingale is not yet an inverse-profile barrier
statement: Irreversible source entry with genuine allocated entry/progress clocks and bounded batches yields deterministic-time target scale n T^(L+1), even with correlated entry collateral, after actual midpoint cohort selection and participation bound B/T. A counterexample uniformly resets one old worker per entry, with per-worker participation gamma C/Y; exact factorial survival (a-1)_j/(y-1)_j shows old targets diluted. At T=a^2/n, progress/kill costs vanish in stated epsilon<1/4 regime but alive inverse-profile stays bounded away from zero while f_s(A0) tends to zero. This disproves population-uniform incoming A-ONLY inverse-profile bound, not earlier constant-adverse-rate contracts. Z(Y-1) is exact entry/reset martingale and progress raises A(Y-1), but nonlinear jump terms remain; no completed incoming barrier, Green scale, signed feedback or full section theorem follows.

requires: Genuine non-double-counted allocated progress subgenerators, collateral safety, bounded adverse batch size and actual per-label predictable participation; regularity/nonexplosion for Dynkin localization.

Each theorem retains its own fixed-population or admissible immigration/pure-deletion seed contract, actual first-terminal stopping and output loss, frozen ordinary labels, exact trace clock and reward-weighted potential.

Uniform/null-slot reset and without-replacement sampling laws for exact carried profiles; a matching mean alone is insufficient. Abstract control converses require free nonnegative finite-rate intensities with no common upper bound.
